option_relations.rationale: The patient's history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and the presence of diffuse medium masses in the right atrium, as well as increased metabolic activity along the right atrial myocardium, suggest recurrent cardiac infiltration of the lymphoma, which is equivalent to cardiac lymphoma.
Secondary cardiac lymphoma can be considered a subtype of cardiac lymphoma, as it refers to lymphoma that has spread to the heart from another location.
Restrictive cardiomyopathy can be a complication of cardiac lymphoma, as the infiltration of lymphoma cells can lead to scarring and stiffening of the heart muscle.
Pericardial involvement with metastatic disease can be considered a subtype of lymphomatous pericarditis, as it refers to the spread of lymphoma to the pericardium.
